name: SPLICE
desc: SPLICE insertion, deletion, and replacement of JSON values; integer, negative, and append offsets; positive, negative, and null counts; pre-edit replacement evaluation; logical cloning; nested and stash arrays; invalid paths and operands; and SPLIT separator and trimming metadata. Error flags allow runtime failures and stronger diagnoses justified by static analysis. No resource limits or optional features are required.

tests.name: Runtime errors and static diagnoses
tests.desc: Replacement evaluation failures abort the splice; permitted static diagnoses do not change explicit FAIL semantics.

tests.name: Cannot read a missing replacement source
tests.desc: Every replacement is evaluated even when the removal count is zero.

tests.name: Cannot read an append position as a replacement
tests.desc: Replacement references must exist in the original array.

tests.name: Later replacement failure aborts the splice
tests.desc: All replacements must evaluate successfully before any alteration. No partial-result shape is mandated.

tests.name: Missing count reference is INVALID_TARGET
tests.desc: Reading an absent property fails before count validation.

tests.name: Intentional failure in count is not upgraded
tests.desc: Explicit FAIL expressions remain INVALID_TARGET even when known statically.

tests.name: Intentional failure in a replacement is not upgraded
tests.desc: Explicit FAIL expressions remain INVALID_TARGET.

tests.name: Intrinsically failing replacement may be diagnosed statically
tests.desc: LENGTH of a number always fails, independently of the input array.

tests.name: Previous replacement action can prove a range failure
tests.desc: The first action guarantees an empty array, so the positive removal count can never succeed.

tests.name: Literal constant count expression can be rejected statically
tests.desc: NOT true always yields false, which is an invalid count rather than zero.

tests.name: Cannot splice a read-only constant array
tests.desc: CONST is read-only; a write attempt is an invalid operand that may be rejected statically.
